limitations: Single engine-assisted reviewer. References use ordinary root lines and played replies before reviewing candidate outputs. Uncertainty is explicit.

cases.rationale: Black can take the c6 pawn but doing so gives White time for Rb7 or Rxg7. The resulting activity and the g-pawn explain why both branches tolerate the capture.
Nf7 gives Black time to eliminate the h6 passer. The other moves give White the timing to mobilize f5 and the king. The captures and the king geometry both matter.
The b3 pawn can be removed by a knight or queen after different move orders. Black uses the time for Nf4 and kingside pressure. All three scores stay close.
Capturing on d6 helps restrain White's advanced pawns. Nc8 allows b7 and the concrete bxc8 bishop promotion after tactical exchanges.
Re8 lets Black use the tempo from the advanced d2 pawn to take the bishop on e4. The other moves let White take d2 with a different material and rook outcome.
Queen or rook promotion gives the same forced liquidation on b1. Bishop promotion changes the concrete result. The immediate promotion choice is the main calculation.
Re8 and Nf6 followed by Ne8 control the approach to promotion. Rf8 permits the forcing e7 and e8 sequences, with a materially worse outcome.
e7 preserves the promotion threat, but Black can meet it by capturing on c5 with check later and then taking e7. The alternative rook moves change the sequence and counterplay.
Black's a-pawn ties down White's rook and balances the central e-pawn. The leading lines handle those targets with different timings, with insufficient evidence of a specific forced tactic.
The b-pawn and a-file constrain Black. Re4+ keeps the rook active, and Re2 allows a forcing sequence in which the rook has to give itself up on b8.
White's d6 pawn restricts Black and remains a target while the bishop and rooks trade. The exchange on f8 and the alternate liquidation on f3 both require concrete calculation.
The b-pawn can be removed on b6 or allowed to reach c7. The latter choice creates a forcing promotion exchange, while Black's rook and minor pieces manage different long-term targets.
